claim_traces.claim_title: US Congress passed no budget on time since 1997
claim_traces.claim_text: "The US Congress has not passed a complete federal budget on time since 1997."
reasoning_steps: According to historical records from the Congressional Research Service (CRS) and analyses by organizations such as the Pew Research Center, the last time Congress enacted all regular appropriations bills prior to the start of the fiscal year was for Fiscal Year 1997 (which began on October 1, 1996)
Under the Congressional Budget Act of 1974, Congress is intended to pass all 12 regular appropriations bills by the October 1 deadline

Since FY 1997, Congress has consistently relied on continuing resolutions (stopgap spending measures) or omnibus packages passed well after the start of the fiscal year to fully fund the federal government.

claim_traces.claim_title: Lightning never strikes the same place twice
claim_traces.claim_text: "Lightning never strikes the same place twice."
reasoning_steps: The claim that "lightning never strikes the same place twice" is a well-known scientific myth
According to atmospheric scientists, the National Weather Service (NWS), and NOAA, lightning frequently strikes the exact same location multiple times
Tall, isolated, and conductive objects (such as skyscrapers, towers, and trees) are struck repeatedly; for example, the Empire State Building is struck by lightning an average of 25 times each year
Furthermore, a single lightning flash often consists of multiple strokes following the identical ionized channel in rapid succession.

claim_traces.claim_title: The Moon is drifting away from Earth
claim_traces.claim_text: "The Moon is slowly moving away from Earth at a rate of about 3.8 centimeters per year."
reasoning_steps: The claim is scientifically accurate and widely documented

Data from the Lunar Laser Ranging experiment—which bounces lasers off retroreflectors left on the Moon by Apollo missions—has precisely measured that the Moon recedes from Earth at an average rate of approximately 3.78 to 3.8 centimeters (about 1.5 inches) per year

This gradual recession occurs because tidal friction created by the Moon's pull on Earth's oceans slows Earth's rotation and transfers angular momentum into the Moon's orbit, pushing it slowly outward.

search_results.snippet: Over time, the Moon has slowly pulled on Earth’s oceans, creating friction that has gradually slowed down the Earth’s rotation. In return, the Moon is slowly moving away from Earth at a rate of about 3.8 centimeters per year.
